issues.body: `NON_VERDICT_CONCLUSIONS = {"cancelled"}` makes `newest_concluded_run` skip every cancelled run solely from its conclusion. The motivating non-verdict is narrower: a concurrency-cancelled run with `jobs.total_count == 0` before job creation. A cancelled run that has one or more jobs proves the workflow was ingested and its job graph was created, so it is a valid healthy ingestion verdict. With an older `action_required`/zero-job run followed by a cancelled run that created jobs, this code selects the stale rejection and continues to upsert/hold M4 even though ingestion recovered. The tests only construct cancelled rows without job evidence and therefore cannot distinguish the intended zero-job case from this overbroad rule.
issues.fix_hint: Classify cancellation using job evidence rather than conclusion alone: only treat a cancelled run as non-verdict when its job read establishes zero jobs (and fail closed when that read is unavailable); treat a cancelled run with jobs as affirmative ingestion evidence. Add detector-level tests for an older zero-job `action_required` followed by (1) cancelled/zero jobs, (2) cancelled/nonzero jobs, and (3) cancelled/unreadable jobs, asserting the correct finding and recovery census in each case.
issues.title: All cancelled runs are discarded without checking whether jobs were created

verdict.summary: The self-observation path is carefully bound to repository, workflow, event, and newest run, and its tests exercise both the pure and live wiring. However, the cancelled-run change broadens a measured zero-job concurrency case into a rule for every cancelled run. A cancelled run can have created/executed jobs, which is affirmative evidence that workflow ingestion succeeded. Unconditionally stepping over it can retain an older rejection and keep/reopen the alert after recovery. Because the marquee classification is not sound for the full conclusion class it handles, changes are required.
